Title: Diagnosis of test `testSingleOptionSingleArgument`

Details:
The failing test `testSingleOptionSingleArgument` from `org.apache.commons.cli2.bug.BugCLI158Test` assesses that when parsing command line arguments with defaults and a single option `-b` having one explicit argument, the resulting list of values includes the explicit argument followed by the last default value.

Step 1: The test sets up a parser by calling `createDefaultValueParser` with defaults `{"100", "1000"}`. This method creates an option `-b` with an argument with minimum 0 and maximum equal to the number of default values, and sets the defaults to the list `["100", "1000"]`.

Step 2: The test provides input arguments `["-b", "1"]` to the parser. The intent is that option `-b` is explicitly given a single argument "1".

Step 3: After parsing, the test retrieves the values for `-b` with `cmd.getValues("-b")`. It expects these to be the explicit argument "1" plus the second default "1000". So `"[" + enteredValue1 + ", 1000]"` i.e. `"[1, 1000]"`.

Step 4: The test fails because the actual values list does not match this expectation. This indicates that the defaults are not being properly handled for partially specified arguments.

Step 5: From the parser code, after copying arguments, it creates a `WriteableCommandLineImpl` and calls `group.defaults(commandLine)`.

Step 6: The `GroupImpl.defaults` method iterates over all options, calling `option.defaults(commandLine)` on each.

Step 7: The bug might be in how the default values are applied when some explicit arguments are passed. Possibly the defaults aren't merged correctly with the explicit arguments.

Hence, the crux of the problem seems to be in how the default values are applied to the command line when some explicit option arguments are provided. The test expects the first given argument plus remaining defaults but the implementation might be overwriting or not merging defaults properly.

Next, I will check the `defaults` method of the `Option` implementation to see how defaults are assigned in presence of partial arguments.

Please specify if I should continue investigating `option.defaults` in the related class.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
